text:
Anton Frondell is 19, the third pick in the 2025 draft, and in his first full NHL season the Blackhawks are already using him in big spots, including Connor Bedard's place on the top line on at least one night. He's playing about 16 minutes and has 11 points in 24 games, after nine in a 12-game look last season.

The scoring is honest: four goals on 4.4 expected, no luck in either direction. The concern is the other end of the ice. At five on five Chicago gets just 36% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nine points worse than when he sits, among the lowest marks on the team. Evolving-Hockey saw the same pattern in his short stint last season, but also noted that he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league, which drags any young player's numbers down.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking finds nothing unusual in his nine tracked games: no clear strength or weakness yet. That fits a teenager learning the league on a rebuilding team. Watch his chance share. The points will come with the minutes; the defensive numbers are what tell you he's arriving.
headline: Frondell's points are honest, the chances against aren't
